claims.text: Post-deposition annealing promotes microstructural homogenization and grain refinement in FeNiCrCoCu thin coatings.
Annealing-induced homogenization and grain refinement enhance high-temperature sliding wear resistance.
The wear improvement occurs because the annealed microstructure limits dislocation mobility and localized plastic deformation.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively inhomogeneous microstructure.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating contains residual stress from processing.
Annealing at approximately 700 °C for 1 hour in an inert atmosphere will homogenize and refine the coating microstructure.
Annealing produces a refined, more uniform solid-solution microstructure.
Annealing reduces residual stress and grain size in the coating.
Reduced microstructural heterogeneity and residual stress hinder dislocation mobility during sliding.
Annealing suppresses dynamic recrystallization during high-temperature sliding.
The annealed microstructure produces a more uniform stress distribution during sliding.
A more uniform stress distribution limits localized plastic deformation that would otherwise accelerate wear.
The annealed coating will have higher hardness than the as-deposited coating.
The annealed coating will have a lower high-temperature sliding wear rate than the as-deposited coating.
The annealed coating will show less microscopic deformation during high-temperature sliding.
The predictions apply at approximately 500–700 °C, where thermally activated deformation mechanisms dominate.
Wear and deformation behavior at lower temperatures may differ.
Oxidation can alter the coating microstructure and surface chemistry and thereby affect wear behavior.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in hardness, wear rate, and microscopic deformation relative to an as-deposited control would falsify the proposed dominant mechanism.
